summary.intent: Run a code quality/simplify review on PR 410 (inline upload progress feature) to eliminate redundancy, improve efficiency, and clean up the implementation.
summary.outcome: Multiple issues fixed: extracted shared helpers (createUploadId, isActiveUpload), added same-value guard to updateFileProgress, made cancelFile atomic (cancel+remove), removed redundant setFileComplete, deleted dead useFileUpload hook and uploadFiles function, added FileList selector equality comparator, fixed race-condition guards after cancelFile semantics changed, removed 'cancelled' from status union, and cleaned up WHAT comments. All 23 tests pass with clean type-check.

repo: upload.store.ts uses Zustand v5; the two-arg equality form of the bound hook has TypeScript inference issues — use useMemo + useRef for stable selector results instead of passing an equality function directly.

cancelFile previously only set status to 'cancelled' but left the entry in the Map; after refactor it atomically removes the entry, requiring all 'status === cancelled' race guards to be changed to check for missing entries instead.
useFileUpload hook and uploadFiles service function were completely dead code — no consumers outside each other.
The 'cancelled' status in PerFileUpload was never actually persisted to the store; it was only used as a transient signal via Axios CancelToken message strings.
FileList was deriving a new array every render from the Map selector with no equality comparator, causing unnecessary re-renders on every upload tick.
useDropUpload subscribed to the entire upload Map just to derive a boolean isUploading, causing broad re-renders on every progress update.

code.finding: updateFileProgress cloned the entire Map on every progress tick with no same-value guard; adding an early return when loaded/total are unchanged eliminates unnecessary downstream notifications during rapid progress events.

Race-condition guards checking 'status === cancelled' broke silently after cancelFile became atomic (delete instead of status set); missing entry (undefined?.status) evaluates to false, not 'cancelled', so guards must check !files.get(uploadId) instead.

Zustand v5 bound hook TypeScript overloads don't infer the two-arg equality form cleanly; idiomatic fix is useMemo with useRef-based deep equality rather than passing a comparator as second arg to the store hook.
useQuotaStore import became unused after uploadFiles was removed; was only referenced inside that dead function.

workflow: Changing the semantics of a store action (cancelFile: status-set → delete) requires auditing all call sites and guards that relied on the old behavior, including race-condition checks that are easy to miss.
Running type-check before tests surfaces import/type issues early; in this session tsc caught the Zustand equality overload problem before tests ran.
Zustand v5 shallow utilities (useShallow) help with object selectors but not with arrays of objects; useMemo + useRef is the reliable fallback for custom equality.

friction: Zustand v5 TypeScript types don't expose a clean two-arg equality overload on the bound store hook, requiring multiple investigative steps (checking node_modules types, version, available exports) before landing on the useMemo/useRef workaround.

The second 'status === cancelled' occurrence at line 153 in useDropUpload.ts had different indentation than the first, causing the Edit tool's first replacement to silently miss it and requiring a re-read + second attempt.
cancelFile semantic change had a non-obvious ripple effect on the FileList filter (which previously filtered out 'cancelled' entries) that had to be caught separately after the main fix.
open_items: Map cloning overhead in updateFileProgress (new Map on every set()) was noted as acceptable at current scale but could be revisited if upload concurrency increases significantly.
File object retention in the store (keeping the full File reference for retry) was intentionally left — could be replaced with a lighter metadata-only structure if memory becomes a concern.

useFileUpload dead code removal was initially skipped as 'may be intentional API surface' before being confirmed dead and removed; worth auditing other hooks/exports for similar orphaned public API surface.

'cancelled' status string still appears in Axios CancelToken message strings as a convention marker even though it's no longer in the PerFileUpload type union — the coupling is implicit and undocumented.
